properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Neches River Near Alto affecting Houston, Angelina, Anderson and
Cherokee Counties.

For the Neches River...including Alto...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Neches River near Alto.

* WHEN...From Friday morning to Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Boat ramps and picnic areas near the river
will begin to flood. Ranchers should move cattle and equipment near
the river to higher ground.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 4.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage Friday
morning to a crest of 16.4 feet early Saturday morning. It will
then fall below flood stage late Saturday evening.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Do not drive cars through flooded areas. Caution is urged when
walking near riverbanks. Turn around, don't drown when encountering
flooded roads. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles.

through flooded areas.

address into your favorite web browser URL bar:

properties.description:
TORCTP

The National Weather Service in State College PA has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Northeastern Bedford County in south central Pennsylvania...
Southern Blair County in central Pennsylvania...
South central Cambria County in central Pennsylvania...

* Until 830 PM EDT.

* At 753 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located over Ski Gap, moving east at 45 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed.
Damage to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree
damage is likely.

* This dangerous storm will be near...
Ski Gap, Roaring Spring, and Claysburg around 800 PM EDT.
Martinsburg around 810 PM EDT.

Other locations impacted by this tornadic thunderstorm include
Woodbury, Spring Hill, Cassandra, Saxton, and East Freedom.

This includes Interstate 99 from mile markers 13 to 27.
properties.instruction:
TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest
floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a
mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter
and protect yourself from flying debris.

Heavy rainfall may hide this tornado. Do not wait to see or hear the
tornado. TAKE COVER NOW!

Tornadoes are extremely difficult to see and confirm at night. Do not
wait to see or hear the tornado. TAKE COVER NOW!

CMAMtext: NWS: TORNADO WARNING in this area til 8:30 PM EDT. Take shelter now. Check media.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: TORNADO WARNING in this area until 8:30 PM EDT. Take shelter now in a basement or an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building. properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 3 at 8:13PM EDT until September 4 at 12:15AM EDT by NWS Pittsburgh PA
properties.description:
FFWPBZ

The National Weather Service in Pittsburgh has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Allegheny County in southwestern Pennsylvania...
Northern Washington County in southwestern Pennsylvania...
Northwestern Westmoreland County in southwestern Pennsylvania...
Southwestern Armstrong County in west central Pennsylvania...
Southeastern Butler County in west central Pennsylvania...
Southern Beaver County in western Pennsylvania...
Brooke County in northern West Virginia...
Hancock County in northern West Virginia...

* Until 1215 AM EDT.

* At 813 PM EDT, local law enforcement and doppler radar reported
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
1.5 and 3 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts
of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Pittsburgh, Penn Hills, Mount Lebanon, Bethel Park, Ross Township,
McCandless Township, Monroeville, Moon Township, McMurray, Weirton,
McKeesport, Franklin Park, Aliquippa, Canonsburg, Gastonville,
Shaler Township, Plum, West Mifflin and North Side Pittsburgh.

Water rescues were reported along Mifflin, Saw Mill Run, and Library
roads. In addition, flash flooding is possible at Pine Creek and
Turtle Creek. Additional heavy rain is expected to move across the
warned are this evening.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 3 at 8:01PM EDT until September 3 at 8:30PM EDT by NWS State College PA
properties.description:
At 801 PM EDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line from
near Duncansville to near Berlin, or along a line from near
Hollidaysburg to 13 miles southeast of Somerset, moving east at 45
mph.

HAZARD...70 mph wind gusts and small hail.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported. At 749 PM EDT a 59 MPH wind gust
was recorded at KJST.

IMPACT...Expect considerable tree damage. Damage is likely to mobile
homes, roofs, and outbuildings.

Locations impacted include...
Johnstown, Somerset, Westmont, Windber, Ebensburg, Bedford,
Belmont, Nanty-Glo, Portage, Breezewood, Warfordsburg, Roaring
Spring, Geistown, Southmont, Berlin, Clearville, New Enterprise,
Martinsburg, Everett and Cresson.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 70 between mile markers 147 and 170. The Pennsylvania
Turnpike between mile markers 108 and 185. Interstate 99 between mile
markers 0 and 26.
properties.instruction:
Anyone outdoors should move to shelter inside a well-built structure
and stay away from windows. These storms have produced widespread
damaging winds.

Tornadoes can develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Seek shelter
immediately in an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built
structure.

Continuous cloud to ground lightning is occurring with these storms.
Lightning is one of nature's leading killers. Remember, if you can
hear thunder, you are close enough to be struck by lightning.

Wind damage with these storms will occur before any rain or
lightning. Do not wait for the sound of thunder before taking cover.
Seek shelter immediately inside a sturdy structure and stay away from
windows.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 3 at 4:50PM CDT until September 5 at 4:28PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Moderate to Major severity and
increased in duration for the following rivers in Texas...

Menard Creek near Rye affecting Polk, Hardin and Liberty Counties.

For the Menard Creek...including Rye...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Menard Creek near Rye.

* WHEN...Until Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 28.0 feet, Major lowland flooding begins with
widespread inundation of the floodplain in the vicinity of the
gage.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:15 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 27.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 17.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:15 PM CDT Thursday was 27.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 28.2 feet
this evening. It will then fall below flood stage early Saturday
morning.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 04/21/1979.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
